analyzed_vuln.description: After parsing an external entity's optional text declaration, xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate unconditionally assigns `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_CONTENT` at line 12897. This revives a parser already placed in terminal `XML_PARSER_EOF` by an out-of-memory error. In this PoV, allocation of the encoding name in xmlParseEncName fails; xmlErrMemory sets EOF, xmlParseTextDecl correctly returns on EOF, but xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate clears that state and continues into xmlParseContent. The malformed continuation is eventually treated as an element name, and xmlParseNCNameComplex passes an invalid name range to xmlDictLookup, causing the global-buffer-overflow read in xmlDictComputeFastKey. The patch-relevant defect is the missing EOF/error check before setting CONTENT and continuing, not the dictionary hash routine.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The schema fuzz harness supplies virtual entity data and derives a deliberately small allocation limit from the fuzz input. The loaded external XML entity begins with a text declaration containing an encoding name (`<?xml encoding="tSCiI"...`). The injected allocation failure must occur at xmlParseEncName's encoding-name allocation, setting the entity parser to EOF. Additional malformed bytes beginning with start-tag-like content must remain so that, after xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate incorrectly resets EOF to CONTENT, parsing reaches xmlParseNCNameComplex with an invalid input/name range. xmlDictLookup then hashes that range and performs the observed out-of-bounds global read.
